This is an appeal (FIRST) filed by appellant under section 14-A(2) of Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 for grant of bail in connection with Crime No.599/2023 registered at Police Station Heera Nagar, District Indore (MP) for offence under Sections 376, 506 of Indian Penal Code, 1860 and also under Sections 3(2)(v) of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989.
2 . T h is appeal under Section 14(A) of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 has been filed against order dated 05.10.2023 passed by Special Judge [under SC/ST(PA) Act] Indore in Special Case / Bail Application No.3622/2023 whereby learned Special Judge rejected the bail application Sunil vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12103918/
1 of appellant.

sentences.text: He is in detention since 31.08.2023.
3. The allegation against the applicant is that of commission of rape with the prosecutrix.
4 . Learned counsel for the appellant has submitted that appellant is innocent and has not committed any offence.
The prosecutrix is a major lady aged 27 years and as per the statement of the prosecutrix recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C she herself has gone with the appellant.
The appellant is in jail since 31.08.2023 and final conclusion of trial will take sufficient long time.

Therefore, it has been prayed that the appellant - accused be released on bail, pending the trial.
5 .
O n the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed the prayer.

6. Having taken into consideration all the fact and circumstances of the case and custody period of the appellant as well as nature of allegation but without expressing any opinion on the merit of the case, I am of the view that it is a case in which further pre-trial detention of the appellant-accused is not warranted.
Consequently, appeal stands allowed.

7. It is directed that appellant be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.

He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C.
8.
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case o f bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.

(PREM NARAYAN SINGH) JUDGE sumathi Sunil vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12103918/
